Adversarially verify this M13 finding. Read the real code (git diff main...HEAD + the file) and try to REFUTE it. Default isReal=false if false positive / pre-existing / out of scope / already handled. Lens:a11y Sev:low File:app/(admin)/admin/users/page.tsx (app/(admin)/admin/users/page.tsx:30-38 (UsersTable render) + components/admin/AdminUserSearch.tsx) Admin user search has no live result-count / no-results announcement AdminUserSearch submits by router.push to /admin/users?q=…, which re-renders the server component and the table in place. There is no aria-live region announcing how many users matched or that none did. The DataTable's emptyText is shown but it sits in a plain , not a live region, so it is not announced after an in-place navigation. This is a regression relative to the codebase's own established pattern: app/(customer)/browse/page.tsx:55-56 wraps its result count in

{t("browse.resultsCount", { count })}

. A blind admin filtering users gets no feedback that the search ran or returned nothing. Suggestion:Add an aria-live="polite" element to the users page showing the result count (e.g. t("admin.usersResultsCount", { count: users.length })) above the table, matching the browse page pattern, with a corresponding en.json key.

content.text:
This fully confirms the finding. The key facts: 1. **BrowseFilters uses `router.push`** (line 21) — the exact same in-place navigation mechanism as AdminUserSearch (line 19). The browse page pairs that with `

{resultsCount}

`. So the browse page is the established pattern for announcing results after a router.push-driven server re-render. 2. **AdminUserSearch has no equivalent.** The admin users page (lines 20-38) renders only `DashboardHeader`, `AdminUserSearch`, and `UsersTable` — no aria-live result count anywhere. 3. **The DataTable's `emptyText` is NOT a live region.** It is rendered in a plain `` (DataTable.tsx lines 137-143). The only aria-live region in DataTable (lines 168-170) is bound to the `announce` state, which is set ONLY by `toggleSort`. It never announces the empty state or row count. So after an in-place navigation that returns zero rows, nothing is announced. 4. There's a `usersNone` key (the table's emptyText) but no `usersResultsCount` key, matching the suggestion that a new key is needed. Let me do one adversarial check: could the router.push cause a full-page reload or focus reset that would naturally announce the content? And is there a page-level heading/landmark change that screen readers announce? Let me verify the DashboardHeader and confirm this is a soft (client-side) navigation.

This confirms the navigation is a Next.js soft navigation (`router.push`), which re-renders the server component tree in place without a full page reload or focus reset. The `<h1>` title ("Manage users") stays constant across searches, so there's no heading change for a screen reader to announce. The static title doesn't change with results, so there's no announcement of how many users matched or whether none did.

I have fully verified every claim in the finding:

- AdminUserSearch uses `router.push` (in-place soft nav) — confirmed (AdminUserSearch.tsx:19)
- No aria-live result-count region on the admin users page — confirmed (page.tsx:20-38)
- DataTable's `emptyText` sits in a plain `<td>`, not a live region — confirmed (DataTable.tsx:137-143)
- DataTable's only aria-live region announces sort changes only, never counts/empty — confirmed (DataTable.tsx:43, 67-69, 168-170)
- The browse page establishes the aria-live count pattern for the identical router.push mechanism — confirmed (browse/page.tsx:55-56 + BrowseFilters.tsx:21)
- The suggested `usersResultsCount` key does not yet exist; `usersNone` exists as emptyText — confirmed (en.json:285)

This is a real, accurate finding. It is correctly scoped as a low-severity a11y issue within M13 (all referenced files are M13 additions per the diff). The only minor caveat is that AdminUserSearch was net-new in M13, so it's not literally a "regression" of pre-existing behavior — but it IS an inconsistency with the codebase's own established browse pattern, which is the substance of the claim. The accessibility gap itself is genuine.
